title: Rerank eval: customer segmentation + stratified sampling for NDCG/MRR pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Improve reranking evaluation fidelity by instrumenting per-customer segmentation and stratified sampling into the NDCG/MRR pipeline so we can detect quality regressions that only surface for specific customer prompt distributions.

Background: Current rerank evals compute aggregate NDCG/MRR across pooled prompt sets. This masks regressions that affect a minority of customers (long-tail prompts, domain shifts). We need to:
  - accept and tag customer prompt sets (obfuscated IDs) in the eval harness,
  - maintain privacy guarantees for customer data ingestion,
  - stratify samples by prompt traits (length buckets, domain tag, percent-of-rephrases),
  - track per-segment NDCG/MRR and surface alerts for regression thresholds, and
  - wire A/B hooks so canary traffic and dedicated rerank variants are scored against identical prompt strata.

Acceptance criteria:
  1) Eval pipeline accepts customer promptsets as CSV/Parquet with metadata and stores obfuscated customer_id tag.
  2) Stratified sampler implemented: discrete buckets for length, doc-count, recency, and domain tag; configurable sampling ratios per project.
 3) NDCG/MRR is computed per-segment and exported to telemetry with stable metric names: rerank.ndcg.segment.{segment_name}, rerank.mrr.segment.{segment_name}.
 4) Dashboards show baseline and delta for each customer segment, with anomaly detection alerting when delta < -0.05 NDCG for 3 consecutive runs.
 5) A/B testing hooks: eval harness can label examples by experiment arm and produce arm-specific segment metrics.
 6) Data privacy: customer IDs are hashed with per-tenant salt and ingestion pipeline documents retention rules.

Design notes / trade-offs:
  - Sampling: we favor stratified sampling to lower variance in segment metrics; full re-ranking of very large promptsets is expensive, so default sample size is 5k per segment with configurable overrides.
  - Privacy: hashing + salt keeps identifiers unlinkable across projects; we avoid storing raw prompts in the central eval DB. For high-security customers, we support an encrypted S3 bucket ingestion path.
  - Latency vs. fidelity: to keep nightly evals within time budget, heavy segments (long sequences) are sampled less frequently but included in weekly full-run.
  - Backfill: this ticket includes a one-time backfill plan for the last 12 weeks of eval runs for affected customers to populate baselines.

Implementation plan:
  - Phase 1 (this ticket): implement ingestion contract, obfuscation, stratified sampler, and per-segment metric emission. Add unit/integration tests.
  - Phase 2: dashboard and alerting, A/B arm tagging, and sample-size tuning.
  - Phase 3: backfill, documentation, and runbook for interpreting per-segment regressions.

Rollout plan: start with internal canaries (team-owned prompt sets), then opt-in pilot with two customers (legal signoff on prompt ingestion), then wide rollout to all evals.
